title: Endpoint reliability contract and prioritized circuit-shedding schedule for multi-region conversational routes
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Production conversational routes have highly variable tail latency and quality sensitivity that make naive SLOs brittle during regional congestion and model rollouts. This ticket defines a per-endpoint reliability contract (SLIs + SLOs + error budget policy) and a prioritized circuit-shedding schedule that is KV-cache and variant-aware for multi-region deployments.

Goal: Deliver a concrete, operational SLO declaration format for conversational endpoints, a set of guardrail thresholds for circuit breakers and load-shedding tiers, and a schedule that ranks variants/routes for graceful degradation in overload scenarios. The artifact must be actionable by the orchestration layer (routing/eviction) and by on-call responders (runbook links).

Scope:
- SLI definitions (latency quantiles, availability, model-quality eval pass rate) per endpoint and per model-variant.
- Error budget burn and automated escalation thresholds (soft throttle, canary rollback, regional failover).
- Prioritized shedding schedule: rules that consider tenant weight, pinned variants, KV cache hit rate, and quality-sensitivity.
- Circuit breaker config templates for region and node-level failures.
- Observability dashboards and synthetic promptset evaluation hooks.

Out of scope: Pricing changes, Dedicated autoscaling policies, and non-conversational multimodal endpoints (handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLO declaration document created and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML (contains SLI formulas and sampling windows)
Circuit breaker templates (region and node) committed to config repo and used in simulation harness
Prioritized shedding schedule implemented as a policy CRD and tested in the staging chaos experiments with clear degradation ordering
Dashboards with per-endpoint SLI heatmaps exist and display live burn-rate and per-variant attribution
Runbook updated with automated remediation steps for each error budget threshold (soft throttle, evacuate-region, rollback variant)
Security sign-off obtained because contract references tenant metadata and routing policies
tasks: Draft SLI formulas: p50/p95/p99 latency (inferred tail metric), availability (5xx + timeouts), quality SLI using promptset pass rate
Define SLOs and error budget windows (daily/weekly) and burn thresholds for automated actions
Design circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis for region/node levels
Implement prioritized shedding policy in orchestration layer (policy CRD) and wire into routing decision path
Add SLI attribution tags for variant, tenant, route, region, cache-hit to telemetry pipeline
Create dashboards and synthetic promptset evaluation runner and hook to alerts
Run staged chaos tests (network degradation, GPU OOM, KV cache miss surge) and collect results
Author runbooks and postmortem template for error budget exhaustion events

decisions: Use p99 latency (tail) and availability (requests not completed within timeout or 5xx) as primary SLIs for hard SLOs
Quality SLI will be promptset-based pass rate with intent buckets; use weighted composition when computing composite endpoint SLO

Error budgets tracked on 24h rolling window and weekly aggregated for trend detection; automated actions at 10% burn (soft throttle), 30% (regional fallbacks), 60% (eviction of low-priority variants), 90% (operator alert + emergency rollback)
Circuit-breaker hysteresis: trip after 30s sustained violation, backoff evaluation every 60s with exponential cool-down up to 10m
Shedding order factors: pinned variants (highest), tenant SLA tier, KV cache hit-rate (+20% priority boost), model quality-sensitivity, cost-per-token (tie-breaker)
Policy will be expressed as a CRD consumed by router with deterministic scoring so behavior is reproducible in tests
